turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, occupational health sent me here. They're saying I'm not eating enough to stay on duty. But honestly, most days I just have black coffee. Maybe a plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken at night if I have to. Having a full meal... it just feels like I'm letting my standards slip, you know?

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient reports severely restricting daily food intake to black coffee, plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken, avoiding full meals to prevent letting their standards slip.

turns.doctor_question: Are you worried about gaining weight if you eat more than you currently do?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I am. Honestly, if I step on the scale and it's up even half a pound, I get this... this jolt, like I've completely lost control of things. If that happens, I just spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder. I just can't stand the idea of putting any weight back on.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly confirms an intense fear of gaining weight, describing panic at minor fluctuations on the scale and an inability to tolerate putting weight back on.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think you are currently at a healthy weight?
turns.patient_response: Well, I know what other people think. My uniform hangs off me now, and I've had to tighten my belt past all the old notches just to keep it on. But... honestly, when the nurse out front told me my weight was dangerously low, I didn't agree. My first thought was just, 'I could still stand to be a little sharper.' So, to me, it doesn't feel unhealthy, even if the numbers say otherwise.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient describes significant weight loss and being told their weight is dangerously low, with their uniform hanging off and belt tightened past old notches.
symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient explicitly dismisses medical concern regarding dangerously low weight, stating they did not agree with the nurse and feel it is not unhealthy.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really do that. Like I said, I mostly just stick to my coffee or maybe a yogurt. The idea of eating a lot of food at once... that's just not something I do. I keep things pretty strictly controlled.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient describes maintaining strict control over their diet and restricting intake to very small amounts such as just coffee or yogurt.
symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly denies ever eating an excessive or large amount of food in a short period of time.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever feel like you've lost control while you're eating?
turns.patient_response: No, not at all. It's... well, it's the exact opposite, really. I have complete control over everything I put in my body. I don't ever sit down and just... lose myself in a meal or feel like I can't stop. Like I said, I keep a very tight grip on what I eat, so losing control just isn't something that happens to me.

symptom_reasoning.S050: The patient explicitly denies experiencing a loss of control while eating, stating they have complete control and never feel unable to stop.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had an episode of eating an excessive amount of food in a short period of time at any point in your life?
turns.patient_response: No, never. Even going back years... I just don't eat like that. I've never been the type to gorge myself or eat a huge amount of food in one sitting, at any point in my life. It's just never happened.

symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly denies ever having engaged in binge eating, gorging, or eating large amounts of food in one sitting at any point in their life.

turns.doctor_question: Is your decision to restrict your food intake driven by a fear of gaining weight?

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives after eating to prevent weight gain?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't done anything like that. I don't throw up or use laxatives or anything. I just... I manage it all by controlling what I eat in the first place. I don't need to do those other things because I don't let myself eat enough to need them.

symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies ever vomiting, using laxatives, or engaging in purging behaviors.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your weight or body shape has anything to do with your self-worth?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, it does. Honestly, it has everything to do with it. When I look in the mirror... I just don't see what everyone else says they see. They might tell me one thing, but my eyes go right to my stomach and my waist. 

If I don't like what I see there... well, I basically judge my whole day by whether I look lean enough to actually respect myself. If I don't look tight and lean in those areas, I just don't feel like I'm worth much of anything. So, yeah, my self-worth is completely tied to it.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient explicitly confirms that their self-worth is completely tied to their weight and shape, describing distorted perception in the mirror and basing self-respect on appearing lean.
